title: GraphQL Schema and Runtime Engineering
centralQuestion: How can clients select graph-shaped data and operations without moving business ownership, authorization, cost, or consistency into an uncontrolled gateway?
responsibility: Design a governed GraphQL schema and runtime that composes service-owned capabilities with bounded execution and truthful partial results.
incomingBoundary: The Course 8 distributed architecture handoff with explicit service, data, contract, and trust boundaries.
outgoingBoundary: Analysis Graph API 1.0, GraphQL September 2025 schema, persisted operation registry, resolver ownership, demand policy, resumable subscriptions, compatibility gates, and platform-publication metadata.
versionState: HTTP, Event, and RPC APIs preserved; Analysis Graph API 1.0 introduced; GraphQL September 2025; graph metadata migrations 001–004.
languageStrategy: one primary implementation track plus one comparative reference track

modules.title: Graph Interface Placement and the Operation Lifecycle
modules.centralQuestion: Where does GraphQL belong, and what happens between receiving a document and returning a response?
modules.capstoneIncrement: Publish the graph boundary and operation-lifecycle trace.
learningOutcomes: place GraphQL without changing service authority
trace parse, validate, admit, execute, complete, and serialize phases
review a field as an architecture edge

modules.title: Type System, Nullability, and Semantic Modeling
modules.centralQuestion: How does the schema make useful promises without promising values the runtime cannot sustain?
modules.capstoneIncrement: Release Analysis Graph API 1.0 type and nullability policies.
learningOutcomes: model lists, interfaces, unions, enums, scalars, and inputs
detect schema promises the runtime cannot keep

modules.title: Resolver Architecture, Batching, and Source Ownership
modules.centralQuestion: How can nested graph execution remain faithful to service ownership without producing N+1 calls?
modules.capstoneIncrement: Replace N+1 nested calls with request-scoped batching.
learningOutcomes: map every field to one source

modules.title: Queries, Identifiers, Connections, and Pagination
modules.centralQuestion: How can clients navigate lists and relationships without unstable pages, leaked internals, or unbounded work?
modules.capstoneIncrement: Implement global IDs and stable, bound connections.
learningOutcomes: bind cursors to tenant and filters

modules.title: Mutations, Idempotency, Concurrency, and Domain Results
modules.centralQuestion: How do graph mutations preserve the durable command guarantees of the owning service?
modules.capstoneIncrement: Expose idempotent create/start/cancel mutations over owning services.
learningOutcomes: model domain results separately from execution errors

modules.title: Authorization, Tenancy, and Schema Exposure
modules.centralQuestion: How can clients select flexible fields without gaining flexible authority?
modules.capstoneIncrement: Prove field, tenant, collection, and sensitive-output authorization.
learningOutcomes: choose an introspection and trusted-document policy

modules.title: Demand Control, Persisted Operations, and Caching
modules.centralQuestion: How can a client-shaped query language remain bounded under adversarial and accidental demand?
modules.capstoneIncrement: Admit only bounded trusted operations and record cost evidence.

modules.title: Errors, Partial Data, Consistency, and Observability
modules.centralQuestion: How does the graph tell the truth when some fields succeed, some fail, and some are stale?
modules.capstoneIncrement: Return truthful partial data with path-specific errors and traces.
learningOutcomes: use error paths and stable codes
trace graph execution without cardinality explosions

modules.title: Subscriptions, Resume, and Incremental Delivery
modules.centralQuestion: How can real-time graph results remain authorized, bounded, and recoverable across disconnects?
modules.capstoneIncrement: Deliver resumable run updates with gap and duplicate handling.
learningOutcomes: map durable events to subscription responses

modules.title: Schema Evolution, Federation, Governance, and Final Defense
modules.centralQuestion: How does the graph evolve without breaking clients, erasing service ownership, or becoming an ungoverned platform?
modules.capstoneIncrement: Approve Graph API 1.0, reject breaking candidates, and publish Course 10 handoff.
learningOutcomes: classify schema evolution by client direction
